item.title: GOP picks leaders, blocks Hegseth impeachment
item.description: House and Senate Republicans held internal elections for their leadership teams on Tuesday as they prepare to become the minority in January.

item.title: At least 3 killed when SUV crashes into North Hollywood food stand
item.description: At least three people were killed and three others injured when an SUV crashed into a food stand near a Metro bus stop in North Hollywood.

item.title: Matthew Farwell convicted of killing Sandra Birchmore, unborn child
item.description: A jury has found former Stoughton, Massachusetts, police officer Matthew Farwell guilty of killing Sandra Birchmore and her unborn child.

item.title: Meghan Markle's father jailed after cutting off monitoring device
item.description: Thomas Markle was jailed in Florida on Tuesday after federal prosecutors allege that he cut off his location monitoring device earlier in the day.

item.title: Mississippi Senate race leans Democratic; Colom holds narrow lead
item.description: The Senate race in deep-red Mississippi remains unresolved, as Democrat Scott Colom has mounted a surprisingly competitive challenge to incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

item.title: Mississippi Senate election results could come as soon as Friday
item.description: A week after the midterm elections, the Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remain uncalled, but official results for Mississippi could be released as soon as Friday. CBS News' Mark Strassmann reports.

item.title: Kennedy family members join lawsuit to block Trump's arch
item.description: Several members of the Kennedy family have joined the legal battle to prevent President Trump from building a large triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: Top lawyer in DOJ's Civil Division is latest in string of resignations
item.description: The top lawyer in the Justice Department's Civil Division resigned on Monday, marking the latest in a wave of departures since the midterm elections.

item.title: NASA recruiting new astronauts, deadline to apply set for early December
item.description: Astronaut Nichole Stilwell joins "The Daily Report" to discuss job requirements and her experience in space amid a new recruiting push by NASA, with applications closing on Dec. 3.

item.title: Nvidia board names pick for Huang investigation after affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Nvidia's board announced Tuesday that Joon H. Kim, former acting U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York, will lead the company's independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang following his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Shivaram Rajgopal, professor of accounting and auditing at Columbia Business School, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: First day of Russia-Ukraine-U.S. peace talks were constructive, Zelenskyy says
item.description: Trilateral peace talks between the U.S., Ukraine, and Russia are underway in Abu Dhabi, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressing positivity following day one of negotiations on Tuesday. CBS News contributor Elliot Ackerman has more.

item.title: GLP-1 drugs to carry warning about rare vision-loss side effect, FDA says
item.description: GLP-1 drugs will now carry a warning for a rare, but potentially dangerous side effect that can lead to vision loss, the FDA says. Dr. Rachel Pessah-Pollack joins CBS News' "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Incumbent Maria Elvira Salazar wins Florida's District 27 race, CBS News projects
item.description: Incumbent Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar has won the closely watched race for Florida's 27th Congressional District, CBS News projects.

item.title: House blocks Massie's effort to impeach Hegseth
item.description: GOP Rep. Thomas Massie said Monday he would not bring up another resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

item.title: Nvidia stocks fall for second straight day after CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Nvidia's stock slid further on Tuesday amid CEO Jensen Huang's admission that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. CBS News' Jo Ling Kent has more.

item.title: New inflation report shows prices rose in October
item.description: Consumer prices rose more than economists expected in October, according to the latest CPI report. CBS News MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo has more on that and a new report that shows a drop in national gas prices.

item.title: U.S. Army officer arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia, authorities say
item.description: A senior U.S. Army soldier stationed in the United Kingdom was arrested Tuesday on suspicion of spying for Russia, British police said. CBS News' Eleanor Watson has more.

item.title: Algeria gives warm welcome to delegation from U.S. city that hosted team during World Cup
item.description: Algeria hosted a delegation from Lawrence, Kansas, in an all-expenses-paid trip as a warm thank you for welcoming its national team during the World Cup.

item.title: 2-year-old found alone on Texas road after wandering away from day care
item.description: The parents of a 2-year-old who wandered away from day care and was found alone on a Texas road have released a statement demanding answers. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: First snow of the season is coming to Northeast
item.description: Parts of the Northeast could see their first snowfall of the season later this week, as a cold snap spreads over the eastern half of the U.S.

item.title: More than 200 million brace for coldest temperatures of the season
item.description: Millions are bracing for severe weather as a possible nor'easter is set to bring cold temperatures and the first snow of the season to parts of the northeastern United States. Rob Marciano has the forecast.

item.title: Nvidia shares plummet again amid CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Nvidia's stock fell again on Tuesday, bringing its total two-day losses to nearly $500 million as the company grapples with CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Jo Ling Kent reports.

item.title: Meghan Markle's father back in custody after allegedly cutting off his ankle monitor
item.description: Meghan Markle's father, Thomas Markle, who is facing charges for possessing child sexual abuse material, is back in custody after allegedly cutting off his ankle monitor. Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: Why did Hegseth face an impeachment push? Inside the 8 articles
item.description: The impeachment resolution focuses on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's involvement in some of the most controversial episodes of President Trump's second term.

item.title: 11/10: CBS Evening News
item.description: Republicans spare Hegseth from impeachment; U.S. soldier accused of spying for Russia.

item.title: 911 call reporting frat video: "They set their pledges on fire"
item.description: Columbus police on Tuesday released a report of their preliminary investigation into the alleged hazing incident at Ohio State University's chapter of Sigma Alpha Epsilon.

item.title: Sanders won't back Schumer as Democratic leader
item.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders said Tuesday he won't support Sen. Chuck Schumer as Democratic leader in the new Congress, becoming the most prominent progressive to oppose his candidacy to date.

item.title: 24% of Americans with a credit record are behind on their debts
item.description: More U.S. households are falling into debt as they grapple with medical bills, student loans and other expenses, data show.

item.title: NASA is recruiting new astronauts. Here are the qualifications.
item.description: The space agency is recruiting its next class of astronauts as the U.S. plans a new mission to the moon. Here's the kind of person NASA is looking for.

item.title: Thomas Markle Sr., Meghan's father, arrested in Florida
item.description: It was reported in October that Meghan's estranged father, Thomas Markle, was under investigation by authorities in the Philippines for alleged possession of child sexual abuse materials.
